limitations: Policies developed on overlapping discovery subsets; see per-program split reports. This is not fully held-out validation.
Match means predicted next whole singleton response, not proof that reasoning or task quality can be preserved.
Recorded usage belongs to original calls; avoided usage is a conditional gross estimate. No routing/program/fallback cost or future cache effect is subtracted.
Cached input and reasoning are subsets; never add them again to total tokens.
Coverage-only search reads can add context and hit output caps; excluded from exact totals.
Execution requires opt-in and state/hash checks not reconstructable from historical traces. No deployment savings credited.
Only recognized bash-tool shapes are supported. Unsupported patterns abstain; parser errors are reported, not counted as zero-opportunity traces.
Source-reported costs are metadata, not our spending or independently verified invoices.
No source commands or scripts are executed, and no paid model requests are made.
